definitions.explanation: Refers to everyday, routine circumstances as opposed to special or extraordinary situations. Used both as a noun (normal times) and as an adverb (normally, usually).

examples.japanese: {平生|へいぜい}は{穏|おだ}やかな{人|ひと}だ。
{平生|へいぜい}の{心|こころ}がけが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{平生|へいぜい}から{備|そな}えておけば、{災害|さいがい}{時|じ}にも{慌|あわ}てなくて{済|す}む。
examples.english: If you prepare in normal times, you won't panic during a disaster.

notes:
A somewhat literary or formal synonym for {普段|ふだん} (usually, normally). Emphasizes the contrast between ordinary circumstances and exceptional situations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平生|へいぜい}の{行|おこな}い: everyday conduct
- {平生|へいぜい}の{心|こころ}がけ: one's usual attitude/mindset
- {平生|へいぜい}から: from ordinary times onward (implying habitual preparation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {普段|ふだん}: usually, normally — more common in everyday speech
- {日頃|ひごろ}: on a daily basis, ordinarily — similar formality level
- {平素|へいそ}: ordinarily — even more formal, used in business correspondence

REGISTER:
More literary and formal than {普段|ふだん}. Common in essays, formal writing, and proverbs.
